scenario: 你收到一封 AI-enabled coding interview 的邀请，想先弄清楚这类面试通常分成几种赛制，再决定练习方向。
scenario_en: You receive an AI-enabled coding interview invite and want to identify the interview format before choosing how to practice.
q: AI 编码面试主要分成哪两种赛制？
q_en: What are the two main formats of AI coding interviews?
options: 结构化平台面试和开放式 BYOE 面试
只有算法笔试，没有 AI 参与
系统设计面试和行为面试
电话初筛和现场终面
why: 结构化面试由公司提供平台、AI 和固定题目结构；开放式 BYOE 面试由候选人自带机器、编辑器和 AI 工具并共享屏幕。
why_en: AI coding interviews mainly split into structured platform interviews and open-ended BYOE interviews where you bring your own environment.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  AIInterview[AI coding interview] --> Structured[Structured platform]
  AIInterview --> Open[Open ended BYOE]
  Structured --> Platform[Company tools]
  Open --> Workflow[Your workflow]
options_en: Structured platform interviews and open-ended BYOE interviews.
Only algorithm quizzes, with no AI involved.
System-design interviews and behavioral interviews.
Phone screens and onsite final rounds.

rows: 要求自带设备+共享屏幕

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选人自带日常使用的机器、编辑器和 AI 工具，通过屏幕共享作答的开放式面试形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BYOE means the candidate brings their own machine, editor, and AI tools, and screen-shares while working.

optionExplanations: 对，公司提供环境算结构化，候选人自带机器和工具算开放式，这条分界线就是本题问的两种赛制。
把 AI 编码面试误当成传统算法笔试——这类面试的核心恰恰是有 AI 参与写代码，不是纯手写算法。
系统设计和行为面试是不同的面试环节类型，不是编码面试内部的两种赛制划分。
电话初筛和现场终面说的是招聘流程的阶段先后，不是同一场编码面试里的工具环境差异。
optionExplanations_en: Right — company-provided environment is structured, candidate-provided tools is open-ended; that split is exactly the two formats being asked about.
Confuses an AI coding interview with a plain algorithm quiz — the defining trait here is AI helping you code, not solo algorithm writing.
System design and behavioral rounds are different interview types altogether, not the two format buckets inside a coding interview.
Phone screens and onsite finals describe hiring-process stages, not the tool/environment difference within one coding round.

scenario: 面试邀请里有一个公司提前配置好的 CoderPad 或 HackerRank 链接。
scenario_en: The invite includes a company-preconfigured CoderPad or HackerRank link.
q: 这通常暗示哪种格式？
q_en: What format does this usually signal?
options: 纯行为面试，不写代码
没有 AI 的传统白板题
结构化面试
开放式 BYOE
why: 浏览器平台链接通常意味着公司提供代码库、AI 助手和问题流程，你会在受限环境里工作。
why_en: A preconfigured browser-platform link usually signals a structured interview where the company controls the environment.
whenOtherWins: 如果邀请要求你用自己的机器并共享屏幕，那更可能是开放式 BYOE。
tradeoff: 公司提供环境识别为结构化 vs 候选人自带环境识别为开放式
options_en: A pure behavioral interview with no coding.
A traditional whiteboard problem with no AI.
A structured interview.
An open-ended BYOE interview.

rows: 要求自带设备+共享屏幕

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选人自带日常使用的机器、编辑器和 AI 工具，通过屏幕共享作答的开放式面试形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BYOE means the candidate brings their own machine, editor, and AI tools, and screen-shares while working.

optionExplanations: 平台链接本身就是编码环境的入口，不是纯问答，这个信号排除了不写代码的可能。
这是 AI 编码面试的邀请，公司配好的平台链接会接入 AI 助手，和「没有 AI」正好矛盾。
对，公司预先配置好的浏览器链接就是结构化的典型信号——代码、AI 助手和答题环节都锁定在平台内。
开放式的信号是要求自带机器并共享屏幕，不是收到一个平台链接；收到自带设备的邀请才该往这个方向准备。
optionExplanations_en: The link itself is an entry point into a coding environment, not a pure Q&A, so it rules out 'no coding'.
This is an AI coding interview invite, so the company-configured platform link comes with an AI assistant wired in, which contradicts 'no AI'.
Right — a browser link the company set up ahead of time is the classic structured signal: codebase, AI, and problem flow are all locked into the platform.
Open-ended's signal is being asked to bring your own machine and screen-share, not receiving a platform link — watch for that invite pattern instead.

scenario: 招聘方要求你使用自己的机器、自己的 IDE，并共享屏幕。
scenario_en: The recruiter asks you to use your own machine, your own IDE, and screen-share.
q: 这通常暗示哪种格式？
q_en: What format does this usually signal?
options: 结构化 CoderPad 面试
只做 PR 审查，不写代码
完全没有编码环节
开放式 BYOE 面试
why: 自带机器和工具意味着公司想看你的真实工作流，而不是你适应平台的能力。
why_en: Being asked to use your own machine and screen-share signals an open-ended BYOE interview that evaluates your real workflow.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方同时发了平台链接，应以平台说明为准并向 recruiter 确认。
tradeoff: 看真实工作流识别为开放式 vs 看平台适应识别为结构化
options_en: A structured CoderPad interview.
Only a PR review, with no coding.
No coding at all.
An open-ended BYOE interview.

rows: 要求自带设备+共享屏幕

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选人自带日常使用的机器、编辑器和 AI 工具，通过屏幕共享作答的开放式面试形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BYOE means the candidate brings their own machine, editor, and AI tools, and screen-shares while working.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集成开发环境，也就是你日常写代码用的编辑器软件，例如 VS Code。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IDE is the integrated development environment you normally write code in, like VS Code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把代码改动提交给仓库、请求他人审查并合并的请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PR, or pull request, is a request to review and merge a code change into a repository.

optionExplanations: CoderPad 需要用公司提供的浏览器环境，和「自己的机器、自己的 IDE」这个信号方向相反。
PR 审查只是结构化面试里的一种变体形态，这里的信号跟审查代码变体无关。
自带机器共享屏幕依然要写代码，只是从零开始，不代表编码环节被取消。
对，自带机器、自带 IDE 加屏幕共享，说明公司要评估的是你真实的日常操作习惯，不是平台适应力。
optionExplanations_en: CoderPad needs the company's browser environment, the opposite direction from 'your own machine, your own IDE'.
PR review is just one variant that shows up inside structured interviews; it's unrelated to this bring-your-own signal.
Bringing your own machine and screen-sharing still means writing code, just starting from scratch — coding isn't removed.
Right — your own machine, your own IDE, plus screen share signals the company wants to see your real daily habits, not platform adaptation.

scenario: 你拿到一份笼统写着「AI-enabled interview」的邀请，还没确认是结构化还是开放式。
scenario_en: You receive a vague AI-enabled interview invite and have not confirmed whether it is structured or open-ended.
q: 为什么要在面试前向 recruiter 确认具体格式？
q_en: Why should you confirm the exact format with the recruiter before the interview?
options: 因为可以避免写代码
格式决定工具、题型、节奏和准备策略
因为 recruiter 会直接给你答案
因为格式不会影响练习内容
why: 结构化和开放式的工具约束完全不同，准备错格式会让当天工作流不熟，浪费本该用于解题的注意力。
why_en: The format determines your tools, problem shape, pacing, and prep strategy, so confirming it in advance avoids practicing the wrong workflow.
options_en: Because it lets you avoid writing code.
The format determines tools, problem shape, pacing, and prep strategy.
Because the recruiter will hand you the answers directly.
Because the format doesn't affect what you should practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

optionExplanations: 确认格式和是否写代码无关，两种格式都要写代码。
对，工具、题型、节奏和该练什么全都随格式变化，这正是提前确认格式的价值所在。
recruiter 一般只透露流程信息，不会把解题答案告诉你。
格式恰恰决定该练平台适应还是本地工作流，说「不影响」正好说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Confirming format has nothing to do with avoiding code — both formats involve writing code.
Right — tools, problem shape, pacing, and what to rehearse all shift with format, which is exactly the value of confirming it ahead of time.
Recruiters typically share process details only, not the actual solution.
Format is exactly what decides whether you rehearse platform adaptation or your local workflow — this option has it backwards.

q: 补全两类格式：
q_en: Fill in the two interview formats:
text: {{Structured}} 面试由公司提供平台、AI 和问题结构；{{Open-Ended}} 面试使用你自己的 IDE、AI 工具并共享屏幕。
why: 这一区分决定你接下来该适应平台节奏，还是打磨自己日常的 AI 工作流。
why_en: This distinction decides whether you should adapt to a platform's pace or polish your own daily AI workflow.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集成开发环境，也就是你日常写代码用的编辑器软件，例如 VS Code。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IDE is the integrated development environment you normally write code in, like VS Code.

scenario: 你即将进入一场结构化 AI 编码面试。
scenario_en: You are about to enter a structured AI coding interview.
q: 结构化 AI 编码面试通常具备哪些特征？（多选）
q_en: Which traits do structured AI coding interviews usually have? (Select all that apply.)
options: 公司提供浏览器编码环境
候选人可以随意安装本地插件
公司提供 AI assistant
题目和代码库预先加载
why: 结构化面试的核心是平台预设和工具受限；本地插件自由度通常不是这类面试的特征。
why_en: Structured interviews are defined by a preset browser environment, a provided AI assistant, and a preloaded codebase, not free local plugin access.
options_en: The company provides a browser coding environment.
Candidates can freely install local plugins.
The company provides an AI assistant.
The problem and codebase are preloaded.

rows: 要求自带设备+共享屏幕

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

optionExplanations: 对，公司提供内置浏览器编辑器，这也是判断结构化面试最直观的信号之一。
错，自由装插件属于开放式的特征，结构化平台通常锁死本地工具权限。
对，AI 助手由平台方接入配置，能力和权限都不由你决定。
对，题目和代码库开局即预加载，你从读懂已有代码开始而不是从零起步。
optionExplanations_en: True — the company provides a built-in browser editor, one of the most direct signals of a structured round.
False — free plugin installs are an open-ended trait; structured platforms usually lock down local tool access.
True — the AI assistant is wired in by the platform, so its capability and permissions aren't up to you.
True — the problem and codebase are preloaded at the start, so you begin by reading existing code, not building from zero.

q: 把结构化面试常见三阶段排好：
q_en: Put the common three structured-interview phases in order:
steps: 为更大输入或边界情况优化
修复现有代码里的 bug
在可工作的代码上实现新功能
why: 结构化面试常见流程是先修 bug 建立基线，再加功能验证扩展能力，最后处理规模或边界优化，提前知道能帮你按阶段分配时间。
why_en: The common structured flow fixes a bug first, adds a feature, then optimizes for scale or edge cases, so pacing should follow that order.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Bug[Fix bug] --> Feature[Add feature]
  Feature --> Optimize[Optimize edge cases]
  Optimize --> Explain[Explain tradeoffs]

scenario: 你知道结构化题通常按「修 bug → 加功能 → 优化」三阶段推进。
scenario_en: You know structured problems usually move through three phases: fix a bug, add a feature, then optimize.
q: 这个信息最直接帮助你调整什么？
q_en: What does this information most directly help you adjust?
options: 不需要读现有代码，就能直接改
跳过测试，直接提交代码
把时间留给后续功能和优化阶段
把性能优化提前搬到第一阶段
why: 提前知道题目弧线能帮助你保留时间给后续功能和优化，而不是在修 bug 阶段陷入完美主义。
why_en: Knowing the three-phase arc helps you pace the interview and avoid spending all your time perfecting phase one.
whenOtherWins: 如果题面明确只有单阶段任务，就按实际任务节奏安排，不必强套三阶段。
tradeoff: 提前按弧线分配时间 vs 不知道弧线、按感觉分配时间
options_en: Skipping reading the existing code and jumping straight to changes.
Skipping tests and submitting the code directly.
Saving time for the later feature and optimization phases.
Moving performance optimization forward into phase one.
optionExplanations: 读懂现有代码本来就是修 bug 阶段的前提，不会因为知道弧线就被跳过。
测试属于验证环节，节奏信息不能当作跳过验证的理由。
对，提前知道三阶段弧线，就能把时间留给后面的功能和优化，不在修 bug 上过度打磨。
性能和边界优化通常要等代码先跑通才有意义，放进第一阶段是把顺序搞反了。
optionExplanations_en: Reading the existing code is already a prerequisite of the bug-fix phase; knowing the arc doesn't let you skip it.
Tests are part of verification — pacing knowledge is never a license to skip them.
Right — knowing the three-phase arc up front lets you save time for the feature and optimization phases instead of over-polishing the bug fix.
Performance and edge-case work usually only make sense once the code already runs, so front-loading it into phase one reverses the order.

scenario: 你收到结构化面试邀请，但描述写的不是常见的 build-and-optimize，而是给你一个 PR，让你用 AI 读懂改动并决定是否 approve。
scenario_en: You get a structured interview invite, but instead of build-and-optimize it gives you a PR to inspect with AI and decide whether to approve.
q: 这属于结构化面试的哪种变体？
q_en: Which structured-interview variant is this?
options: PR 审查：读 diff 决定是否 approve
纯逻辑脑筋急转弯，完全不涉及任何代码评审
只做候选人简历背景深挖，完全不看任何代码
只写单条 SQL 查询，不涉及任何代码评审环节
why: PR 审查形态和 build-and-optimize 不同，但仍考相同能力：读代码、判断、验证，以及用 AI 辅助理解 diff。
why_en: The PR-review variant looks different from build-and-optimize but still tests reading code, judgment, verification, and using AI to understand a diff.
options_en: A PR review: read the diff and decide whether to approve.
A pure logic riddle that involves no code review at all.
Only a deep dive into the candidate's resume, without looking at any code.
Only a single SQL query, with no code-review step involved.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把代码改动提交给仓库、请求他人审查并合并的请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PR, or pull request, is a request to review and merge a code change into a repository.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

optionExplanations: 对，给你一份 diff 让你判断能否合并，正是结构化面试里的 PR 审查变体。
脑筋急转弯考不到读代码、判断合并风险这些能力，和场景描述的任务形态不符。
简历深挖不会给你具体 diff，也不涉及代码质量判断，是完全不同的评估环节。
单条 SQL 查询和审查一整份 PR 是不同规模、不同性质的任务。
optionExplanations_en: Right — being handed a diff to judge whether to approve is exactly the PR-review variant of a structured interview.
A logic riddle can't test reading code or judging merge risk, which doesn't match the task described in the scenario.
A resume deep-dive doesn't hand you an actual diff or ask you to judge code quality — a completely different evaluation.
Writing one SQL query is a different scale and kind of task from reviewing a whole PR.

scenario: 结构化面试里，AI 助手和编辑器都是公司预先配置好的，你无法更换。
scenario_en: In a structured interview, the AI assistant and editor are preconfigured by the company and you cannot swap them out.
q: 结构化面试的主要缺点是什么？
q_en: What is the main downside of a structured interview?
options: 可以随意安装任何本地开发插件
题目完全没有任何固定结构
面试官完全看不到你写的代码
被锁定在公司平台和 AI 能力里
why: 如果平台 AI 比你日常工具弱，你也不能随意换，只能调整提示策略去适应它，代价是发挥受限。
why_en: The downside of structured interviews is being locked into whatever platform and AI the company provides, even if it's weaker than your daily tools.
options_en: You can freely install any local development plugin.
The problem has no fixed structure at all.
The interviewer can't see any of the code you write.
You're locked into the company's platform and AI capability.
optionExplanations: 结构化平台通常限制甚至禁止装本地插件，这条说反了。
结构化恰恰以固定的三阶段结构著称，「没有结构」正好和定义矛盾。
你的代码在平台环境里对面试官完全可见，可见性不是这里的问题。
对，平台 AI 就算比你日常工具弱，你也换不了，只能调整提示策略去适应，这是结构化最主要的代价。
optionExplanations_en: Structured platforms usually restrict or block local plugins — this has it backwards.
Structured interviews are defined by their fixed three-phase structure, so 'no structure' contradicts the definition.
Your code stays fully visible to the interviewer inside the platform — visibility isn't the issue here.
Right — even if the platform's AI is weaker than your daily tools you can't swap it, only adjust your prompting to cope; that's the main cost of structured interviews.

scenario: Meta 或 LinkedIn 在正式面试前，给你一个平台 practice session。
scenario_en: Meta or LinkedIn gives you a platform practice session before the real interview.
q: 你应该怎么利用它？
q_en: How should you use it?
options: 跳过，正式当天再学
一定参加，提前熟悉平台 AI 的交互细节
只看邮件里的文字说明
只在本地 IDE 里练相似题目
why: 平台界面和 AI 行为有日常 IDE 没有的细节，提前用半小时熟悉能减少正式面试当天的工具摩擦。
why_en: Take the practice session because the platform's AI interface has quirks your normal IDE doesn't, and thirty minutes upfront saves friction on interview day.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有官方练习环境，就用相近的浏览器沙盒模拟受限平台。
tradeoff: 花时间提前适应平台 vs 把时间留到正式面试再摸索
options_en: Skip it and learn on the actual interview day instead.
Definitely take it, to get used to the platform's AI interaction details.
Only read the text instructions in the email.
Only practice similar problems in your local IDE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集成开发环境，也就是你日常写代码用的编辑器软件，例如 VS Code。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IDE is the integrated development environment you normally write code in, like VS Code.

optionExplanations: 跳过等于把平台特有的界面摩擦全部留到正式当天。
对，半小时的官方练习能让你亲手摸过平台 AI 的交互细节，正式当天摩擦最小。
文字说明代替不了亲手操作一遍界面，手感差异不会因为读过说明就消失。
本地 IDE 练不到平台特有的浏览器编辑器和内置 AI 交互，环境不匹配。

Right — a free thirty-minute official session lets you actually touch the platform's AI interaction quirks, so friction on the day is minimized.

optionExplanations_en: The recruiter won't reveal the standard answer, so this yields no usable prep information.
Right — this list hits every axis that decides your practice target: format, starting point, platform stage, AI limits, and how you'll deliver work, nothing left unasked.
AI's role is accelerating implementation; your judgment and control are still what's evaluated, so this misreads AI's role.
Asking only about difficulty gets a subjective impression, not concrete direction on which environment or tools to practice.

q: 把根据格式调整准备的决策链排好：
q_en: Put the decision chain for format-based preparation in order:
steps: 结构化：练浏览器平台、内置 AI、阶段节奏
从邀请或 recruiter 确认格式
开放式：练本地 IDE、AI 工具、屏幕共享工作流
按确认结果选择最贴近的练习
why: 先确认格式，再选练习；结构化练平台节奏，开放式练自己的工具和交付流程，二者内部顺序可按实际格式展开。
why_en: Confirm the format first, then match practice to it: rehearse platform pacing for structured, or your own tools and delivery flow for open-ended.
tradeoff: 先确认格式再匹配练习 vs 不分格式统一刷题
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Confirm[Confirm format] --> Match[Match practice]
  Match --> Tools[Set tool constraints]
  Tools --> Rehearse[Rehearse pacing]
  Rehearse --> Interview[Interview day]

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集成开发环境，也就是你日常写代码用的编辑器软件，例如 VS Code。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IDE is the integrated development environment you normally write code in, like VS Code.

scenario: 同一个人分别准备了一场结构化面试和一场开放式面试。
scenario_en: The same candidate is preparing separately for one structured interview and one open-ended interview.
q: 结构化和开放式最大的策略差异是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest strategic difference between structured and open-ended formats?
options: 结构化练适应受限平台；开放式练展示真实工作流
结构化不用读代码；开放式不用沟通
结构化不能测试；开放式不能用 AI
两者策略完全相同
why: 两种格式考的核心能力相似，但工具自由度和问题起点不同，所以备战侧重不同：一个练适应，一个练展示。
why_en: The core skills overlap, but structured interviews emphasize adapting to a constrained platform while open-ended ones emphasize showing your real workflow and design.
tradeoff: 练适应受限平台 vs 练展示真实工作流
options_en: Structured practices adapting to a constrained platform; open-ended practices showing a real workflow.
Structured doesn't require reading code; open-ended doesn't require communication.
Structured can't have tests; open-ended can't use AI.
The two strategies are completely identical.

rows: 要求自带设备+共享屏幕

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

optionExplanations: 对，结构化的备战重点是适应受限平台的手感和节奏，开放式则要练到能在全程可见下展示真实的设计与工作流。
两种格式都要读代码，也都需要和面试官沟通，这条把两项能力都错误取消了。
两种格式都需要写测试、都会用到 AI，「不能测试/不能用 AI」不成立。
工具自由度和问题起点完全不同，说「策略完全相同」抹平了这些真实差异。
optionExplanations_en: Right — structured prep focuses on getting comfortable with a constrained platform's feel and pacing, while open-ended prep focuses on showing your real design and workflow under full visibility.
Both formats require reading code and communicating with the interviewer — this wrongly cancels both skills.
Both formats need tests and both use AI — 'no tests / no AI' doesn't hold for either.
Tool freedom and starting point differ completely between the two — calling the strategies identical erases that real gap.

scenario: 你把一场其实是结构化的面试，当成开放式来准备。
scenario_en: You prepare for an interview as open-ended, but it is actually structured.
q: 这样做最可能带来什么问题？
q_en: What problem is this most likely to cause?
options: 本地工具已经太熟悉了，反而会有点不习惯
不熟悉浏览器平台、受限 AI 和多阶段节奏
完全不会安装任何本地开发插件
题目的难度会自动变得简单很多
why: 正式当天工具和 AI 都不是你练的那套，认知负担会挤占本该用于解题和沟通的时间。
why_en: Preparing for the wrong format leaves you unfamiliar with the browser platform, constrained AI, and staged pacing, and that friction steals time from solving the problem.
options_en: Being so familiar with local tools that it actually feels awkward.
Being unfamiliar with the browser platform, constrained AI, and multi-phase pacing.
Not knowing how to install any local development plugin at all.
The problem automatically becoming much easier.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

optionExplanations: 本地工具练得熟练在结构化面试里根本用不上，这不是错配格式带来的问题。
对，正式当天你面对的浏览器平台、受限 AI 和阶段节奏全是没练过的，认知负担会挤占解题时间。
结构化平台本来就通常禁止装插件，这不是错配格式暴露的问题。
题目难度由面试设计决定，不会因为你准备的方向而变化。
optionExplanations_en: Being fluent with local tools simply isn't usable in a structured interview — that's not a consequence of the mismatch.
Right — on the day you'll face an unpracticed browser platform, constrained AI, and staged pacing, and that unfamiliarity eats into time you need for solving the problem.
Structured platforms usually block plugins anyway — that's not what the mismatch exposes.
Difficulty is set by the interview design, not by which direction you happened to prepare.

scenario: 你把一场其实是开放式的面试，当成结构化来准备。
scenario_en: You prepare for an interview as structured, but it is actually open-ended.
q: 这样做最可能漏掉什么？
q_en: What are you most likely to miss by preparing this way?
options: 浏览器平台上按钮的具体位置
内置 AI 助手的具体限制
本地环境、AI 工具和交付流程的完整演练
固定不变的三阶段节奏安排
why: 开放式中你的真实工具链会被完整看见，不提前演练本地环境和交付流程，容易在当天暴露生疏。
why_en: Preparing for the wrong format leaves you without rehearsed local tools, AI setup, repo delivery, or screen-sharing workflow, exactly what open-ended interviews expose.
options_en: The exact layout of buttons on the browser platform.
The specific limitations of the built-in AI assistant.
Rehearsing your local environment, AI tools, and delivery workflow in full.
The fixed, unchanging three-phase pacing arrangement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

optionExplanations: 浏览器平台是结构化才会遇到的界面，开放式根本不会用到公司平台。
内置 AI 的限制同样属于结构化的特征，开放式用的是你自己的工具，不受它约束。
对，你会漏掉本地环境、AI 工具和交付流程的完整演练，而这些正是开放式全程可见下最容易暴露生疏的地方。
固定三阶段节奏是结构化的特征，开放式题目通常没有这种固定结构。
optionExplanations_en: The browser platform is a structured-only surface — open-ended never touches the company's platform at all.
Built-in AI limits are also a structured trait; open-ended uses your own tools and isn't bound by that.
Right — you'll miss rehearsing your local environment, AI tools, and delivery flow, exactly what's most likely to look unpracticed once everything is visible.
Fixed three-phase pacing is a structured feature; open-ended problems usually have no such fixed structure.

q: 补全格式判断口诀：
q_en: Fill in the format-identification rule of thumb:
text: 邀请里有平台链接，多半是{{结构化}}；要求自带机器和屏幕共享，多半是{{开放式}}；不确定就问{{recruiter}}。
why: 这个判断口诀能让你在拿到邀请的第一时间，快速决定该练平台适应还是练自己的真实工作流。
why_en: This rule of thumb lets you quickly decide, right from the invite, whether to practice platform adaptation or your own real workflow.

scenario: Meta 的 AI 编码轮在 CoderPad 上进行：开场有一个模型下拉框（GPT-4o、GPT-5、Claude Sonnet/Haiku、Gemini、Llama），选定后修 bug、加功能、做优化三个阶段都用它，不能换成场外工具。
scenario_en: Meta's AI-enabled round runs on CoderPad: at the start you pick from a model dropdown (GPT-4o, GPT-5, Claude Sonnet/Haiku, Gemini, Llama), and that model carries you through all three phases with no outside tools allowed.
q: 面对这个模型下拉框，最该提前做好的准备是什么？
q_en: Facing that model dropdown, what should you prepare beforehand?
options: 提前用同一个模型练熟，进场直接选它
三个阶段各换一个模型，边做边比出最好用的
不管选哪个都差不多，用默认选中的那个即可
请面试官允许你换成平时用的 AI 工具
options_en: Practice on one specific model beforehand and pick that same one on the spot.
Switch models between the three phases and compare which one works best.
The choice barely matters, so just keep whichever model is selected by default.
Ask the interviewer to let you swap in the AI tool you normally use.
optionExplanations: 对，模型只在开场选一次，把不确定性挪到练习阶段，面试里就只剩解题。
换模型会丢掉之前累积的对话上下文，还要重新试探它的提示词脾气，三个阶段本来就不够用。
候选人反馈平台自带的 AI 弱于自己练熟的工具，随手接受默认等于放弃唯一能自己控制的变量。
结构化面试的定义就是环境和 AI 由公司提供，工具被锁死，这个请求不会被批准。
optionExplanations_en: Right — you pick once at the start, so push the uncertainty into practice and leave only problem-solving for the interview.
Switching loses the conversation context you built up and forces you to re-learn each model's prompting quirks, and three phases are already tight.
Candidates report the platform AI is weaker than what they practiced with, so accepting the default throws away the one variable you control.
A structured round is by definition one where the company supplies the environment and AI, so the tools are locked and this request goes nowhere.
why: 工具锁死是结构化面试的核心约束：模型只选一次、中途换就丢上下文，所以试错必须发生在面试之前。代价是你放弃了临场挑最强模型，换来对它输出风格的确定性。
why_en: In a structured round the tooling is locked, so the model choice happens once and any mid-interview switching costs you context — do the experimenting in practice instead.
tradeoff: 对模型的熟悉度 vs 临场挑到能力最强的模型
whenOtherWins: 如果公司提供了赛前 practice 环境（Meta 和 LinkedIn 都有），在练习场里横向试各个模型就是对的，那时比较不占面试时间。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个浏览器里的在线编码面试平台，Meta 和 LinkedIn 的 AI 编码轮都在它上面进行，代码、AI 聊天面板和题目都预先加载好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a browser-based coding interview platform where the codebase, the AI chat panel, and the problem statement are all preloaded.

termDefinitions.meaning: OpenAI 的一个通用大语言模型，是 Meta CoderPad 模型下拉框里的可选项之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GPT-4o is one of OpenAI's general-purpose large language models, offered as one choice in Meta's CoderPad model dropdown.

termDefinitions.meaning: Meta 自研的开源大语言模型系列，同样出现在他们面试平台的模型选项里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Llama is Meta's own family of open-weight large language models, also listed among the model options in their interview platform.

scenario: Uber 的 AI 编码轮跑在 HackerRank 上，仓库是预置好的：你打开就看到一份从没读过的现成代码，题目要求在它上面做改动，而不是从空目录起步。
scenario_en: Uber's AI-enabled round runs on HackerRank with a pre-set repository: you open it to find existing code you've never read, and the task is to change that code rather than start from an empty directory.
q: 开场头几分钟，该让 AI 先做哪件事？
q_en: In the first few minutes, what should you have the AI do first?
options: 先让 AI 概述仓库结构，定位要改的模块
跳过已有代码，让 AI 按题目描述直接生成新功能
自己逐个文件通读一遍，读懂之后再动用 AI
先让 AI 做性能优化，把最难的部分提前拿下
options_en: Have the AI summarize the repo layout and locate the modules you need to change.
Skip the existing code and have the AI generate the new feature straight from the problem statement.
Read every file yourself first, and only bring in the AI once you understand it.
Have the AI do the performance optimization first, knocking out the hardest part early.
optionExplanations: 对，预置仓库考的就是导航能力，先建立地图才知道改动落在哪里。
这是把 greenfield 的习惯带进了棕地题：AI 会另造一套与现有结构脱节的实现，后面阶段接不上。
把 AI 晾在一边等于自愿放弃这轮面试要考察的能力，而且手读全仓库会烧光第一阶段的时间。
结构化面试的题目弧是先修 bug、再加功能、最后优化，跳到最后一段会在还没跑通的代码上做优化。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a pre-set repo tests navigation, and you need the map before you know where your change lands.
This carries a greenfield habit into a brownfield task: the AI writes an implementation disconnected from the existing structure, and later phases can't build on it.
Sidelining the AI forfeits the very skill this round measures, and hand-reading the whole repo burns all of phase one.
The structured problem arc runs bug fix, then feature, then optimization — jumping to the end means optimizing code that doesn't work yet.
why: 预置仓库把考点从「能不能造」换成了「能不能在别人的代码里落点」，所以第一动作是用 AI 建立结构地图。代价是开场几分钟没有可见的代码产出，要靠讲解让面试官看到你在做什么。
why_en: A pre-set repo shifts the test from can-you-build to can-you-land-a-change in someone else's code, so your first move is using the AI to map the structure.
tradeoff: 先导航已有代码 vs 尽快产出新代码
whenOtherWins: 开放式 BYOE 面试给的是空仓库或一份 README，根本没有已有代码可导航，那时让 AI 按描述直接生成才是正确起手式。

rows: 让 AI 按描述搭骨架

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个在线编码测评平台，Uber 的 AI 编码轮在它上面进行，并预先放好一个仓库让你改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is an online coding assessment platform; Uber runs its AI-enabled round there with a repository already set up for you to modify.

termDefinitions.meaning: 绿地项目，指从空仓库或一份需求文档起步、没有历史代码包袱的开发场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greenfield project starts from an empty repository or just a spec, with no existing code to work around.

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选人自带机器、编辑器和 AI 工具，通过共享屏幕作答的开放式面试形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BYOE means the candidate brings their own machine, editor, and AI tools, and screen-shares while working.

termDefinitions.meaning: 仓库根目录下说明项目做什么、怎么跑的文档，开放式面试常只给这一份作为题面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A README is the document at a repo's root explaining what the project does and how to run it; open-ended rounds often hand you only this as the problem statement.
